# Activity Platform

Two applications: a Vue 3 admin dashboard backed by Laravel 13 and MySQL, and a Go Windows desktop agent with an embedded Vue status/login screen.

## Source package and project layout

The GitHub source ZIP includes all application source, dependency lockfiles, tests, deployment files and compiled Vue assets. It excludes installed dependencies, executables, credentials, runtime databases, employee screenshots and logs. Run the commands below to install dependencies and build the Windows executable. Use Node 22.12+ and PowerShell 7 for the supplied build/packaging scripts.

| Folder | Contents |
| --- | --- |
| `server/` | Laravel API, administrator authentication, migrations, jobs and tests |
| `web/` | Vue administrator dashboard and agent interface |
| `agent/` | Go Windows collector, queue, embedded frontend and tests |
| `deploy/` | Docker, PHP and Nginx configuration |
| `scripts/` | Frontend build, Windows agent build and release packaging |

Choose **Herd** below for Windows development, **Quick local demonstration** for SQLite, or **Docker / MySQL** for containers. Only `web/` needs npm installation; the Laravel skeleton's `server/package.json` is not the dashboard build.

## Windows installation with Laravel Herd

1. Extract the ZIP, preserving the `activity-platform` directory. Install PHP 8.4 in Herd, Node 22.12+, and MySQL (Herd Pro Services or a separate MySQL server). To build the agent, install Go 1.22+ too.
2. In PowerShell, enter the extracted `server` directory and link it:

```powershell
cd C:\Users\YOUR_USER\Herd\activity-platform\server
herd link activity
herd isolate 8.4 --site=activity
herd secure activity
herd composer install
if (!(Test-Path .env)) { Copy-Item .env.example .env }
```

3. Create a MySQL database named `activity_platform`. Edit `server/.env` with your actual database credentials and service port:

```dotenv
APP_ENV=local
APP_URL=https://activity.test
DB_CONNECTION=mysql
DB_HOST=127.0.0.1
DB_PORT=3306
DB_DATABASE=activity_platform
DB_USERNAME=your_mysql_user
DB_PASSWORD="your_mysql_password"
SESSION_SECURE_COOKIE=true
TRACKER_STORAGE=local
```

4. Initialize this new installation. Generate the application key only when APP_KEY is empty; preserve it on upgrades.

```powershell
herd php artisan config:clear
herd php artisan key:generate
herd php artisan migrate --seed
herd php artisan tracker:create-admin admin@example.com
```

5. Open https://activity.test and log in with the administrator account you just created. Run these in two separate terminals in `server/` and keep them running:

```powershell
herd php artisan queue:work --tries=3 --timeout=120
```

```powershell
herd php artisan schedule:work
```

Herd serves the website; `artisan serve` is unnecessary with this option. The release includes built Vue assets. To rebuild the frontend and Windows executable from source, run from the project root:

```powershell
cd web
npm ci
cd ..
node scripts/build-web.mjs
./scripts/build-agent.ps1
```

Copy `agent/agent-config.example.json` to `agent/agent-config.json`, set `server_url` to `https://activity.test`, and start the resulting `agent/activity-agent.exe`. Create an employee in the dashboard and log in through the agent. Monitoring begins after employee login and notice acceptance when policy permits it. The local `.test` address is only for this computer; other machines require a reachable HTTPS deployment.

PHP needs GD for thumbnails and PDO MySQL for MySQL. Set `upload_max_filesize=20M`, `post_max_size=24M`, `memory_limit=512M`, and ensure Nginx permits 24 MB requests. Restart affected Herd services after PHP configuration changes. If a certificate error occurs, repair Herd's local certificate trust rather than disabling TLS verification.

References: [Herd site linking](https://herd.laravel.com/docs/windows/getting-started/sites), [PHP isolation](https://herd.laravel.com/docs/windows/technology/php-versions), [HTTPS](https://herd.laravel.com/docs/windows/sites/securing-sites).

## Implemented

- Real server authentication; employee enrollment; administrator and reviewer roles; disabled accounts and revoked device tokens.
- Live local clock, visible monitoring notice, Windows tray icon and console status.
- One screenshot at a random offset in each 120-second period by default. Captures the combined Windows desktop across monitors. Administrators can change the period.
- Foreground application/process name and window title sampling. Optional browser address capture through Windows UI Automation; URL credentials, query strings and fragments are removed.
- Private screenshot gallery with thumbnails, full-size viewing, employee/device/date/application filters and pagination.
- Searchable activity records and CSV export with spreadsheet formula neutralization.
- Device enrollment, persistent UUID, heartbeats, online status, administrator pause/resume and disable controls.
- Central policy settings for capture interval, application sampling, URL collection, notice, retention and offline queue size.
- HTTPS API ingestion with device-scoped tokens, duplicate detection, explicit upload acknowledgments and validation.
- Private server storage or certificate-verified FTPS. The admin Policy page has a storage write/read/delete verification button. Destination credentials are set in the **server environment**, not distributed to employees or editable in the browser.
- Persistent local outbox, retry delays, restart recovery, per-user ownership, disk limits, expiry and local diagnostic logs. Payloads leave the queue only after acknowledgment or configured retention expiry.
- Windows DPAPI protection for saved login tokens; session login and CSRF protection for the dashboard; role checks and audit records for sensitive access.
- Queued thumbnail generation and scheduled retention cleanup, plus MySQL migrations, Docker deployment files, tests and a Windows executable.

## Quick local demonstration

Requirements: PHP **8.4+**, Composer 2, Node **22.12+**, and MySQL 8.4 for normal deployment. PHP extensions: PDO MySQL, PDO SQLite (tests/demo), mbstring, fileinfo, OpenSSL, cURL, GD, ZIP and Intl. Go 1.22+ is needed only to rebuild the agent.

From this directory:

```powershell
cd web
npm ci
cd ..
node scripts/build-web.mjs
cd server
composer install
Copy-Item .env.example .env
```

Set `DB_CONNECTION=sqlite` in `server/.env`, remove or comment `DB_DATABASE=activity_platform`, and create an empty `server/database/database.sqlite`. Keep `APP_ENV=local`. Then:

```powershell
php artisan key:generate
php artisan migrate --seed
php artisan db:seed --class=DemoSeeder
php artisan serve --host=127.0.0.1 --port=8000
```

Open http://127.0.0.1:8000. Demo accounts are `admin@example.test`, `reviewer@example.test` and `employee@example.test`, all with password `LocalDemo!2026`. They are created **only** by explicitly running DemoSeeder, which refuses production environments. Gallery images are synthetic. Do not seed demo accounts on a real deployment.

Run `php artisan queue:work --tries=3 --timeout=120` and `php artisan schedule:work` in separate terminals during local use. The scheduler is required for retention cleanup.

## MySQL installation

Use `server/.env.example`, create a MySQL database and restricted application user, then set `DB_HOST`, `DB_PORT`, `DB_DATABASE`, `DB_USERNAME` and `DB_PASSWORD`. Set `APP_ENV=production`, `APP_DEBUG=false`, `APP_URL` to your HTTPS origin and `SESSION_SECURE_COOKIE=true`.

```text
composer install --no-dev --optimize-autoloader
php artisan key:generate
php artisan migrate --seed --force
php artisan tracker:create-admin admin@your-company.com
php artisan config:cache
```

The create-admin command prompts privately for a password of at least 12 characters. Add employee and reviewer accounts through Employees in the dashboard. Set the web document root to `server/public`, give the PHP runtime write access to `storage` and `bootstrap/cache`, and keep the queue worker and scheduler running. Configure PHP `upload_max_filesize=20M`, `post_max_size=24M`, `memory_limit=512M` and your proxy's request-body limit accordingly. Do not expose the private storage directory with a public symlink.

## Docker / MySQL

Docker Desktop or Docker Engine with Compose is required. Copy the root `.env.example` to root `.env`, replace both database passwords, and generate a stable Laravel key:

```text
docker compose build
docker compose run --rm --no-deps app php artisan key:generate --show
```

Paste the resulting `base64:...` into root `.env` as `APP_KEY`. Then:

```text
docker compose up -d db app
docker compose exec app php artisan migrate --seed --force
docker compose exec app php artisan tracker:create-admin admin@your-company.com
docker compose up -d web worker scheduler
```

Open http://127.0.0.1:8080. The port is bound to loopback. For remote agents, put an HTTPS reverse proxy in front of it, use the HTTPS `APP_URL`, and set `SESSION_SECURE_COOKIE=true`. Back up the MySQL volume, private-data volume, environment credentials and APP_KEY. Do not regenerate APP_KEY on an existing installation. Deployments must preserve storage permissions for `www-data`.

## Run the Windows agent

1. Build `agent/activity-agent.exe` using the build commands below if using the source-only ZIP. Copy it and `agent/agent-config.example.json` into a writable folder on the employee computer.
2. Rename the configuration to `agent-config.json`. Set `server_url` to your HTTPS server origin (HTTP is accepted only for loopback IPs during development). Set `device_name` or leave it empty to use the Windows hostname.
3. Start `activity-agent.exe`. It opens http://127.0.0.1:8765/agent. Read the monitoring notice and sign in using an employee account.
4. Keep the agent running in the interactive Windows session. The administrator controls policy and device pause. Closing the browser tab does not stop the agent; exiting the console/process or signing out does.

`data/payloads` holds queued PNGs, `data/outbox` holds their manifests and activity events, and `data/logs` holds diagnostic logs. Successful upload removes queued files; retained images live on the server. Token storage is protected by the current Windows account. If Windows DPAPI is unavailable, the agent can run with an in-memory session and requires login after restart. Use Windows account and folder permissions to protect local screenshot files.

Build after changing frontend source:

```powershell
node scripts/build-web.mjs
./scripts/build-agent.ps1
```

The executable embeds the Vue build. Rebuilding Vue alone does not update an existing executable. The binary is unsigned. Automatic startup, MSI installation and tamper-resistant Windows service management are not included.

## FTPS storage

Default `TRACKER_STORAGE=local` writes to private Laravel storage. To use FTPS, set these on the Laravel server and restart workers / refresh cached configuration:

```dotenv
TRACKER_STORAGE=ftps
TRACKER_FTPS_URL=ftp://files.example.com/tracker/
TRACKER_FTPS_USERNAME=your-service-account
TRACKER_FTPS_PASSWORD=your-secret
TRACKER_CURL_BINARY=curl
```

`ftp://` uses explicit TLS (`--ssl-reqd`); `ftps://` uses implicit TLS. Certificates must be trusted. The service account needs create, read, write, list and delete permissions. Use **Policy → Verify storage connection** before enabling monitoring. Failed FTPS writes are not acknowledged, so the agent retains the upload for retry. The agent always sends to Laravel's API, which handles the FTPS destination. Arbitrary third-party upload APIs and plaintext FTP are not supported.

Existing FTPS records refer to the configured destination. Do not change its host/base folder while retained files remain there without migrating those files. Server credentials must never be included in a source archive or employee config.

## Validation and known limits

Verified in this workspace: Laravel feature suite (17 tests, 73 assertions), Go queue/client tests (12 tests), Go vet/build, Vue production build and frontend utility tests (2). Browser checks use the local SQLite demonstration. Run tests yourself with `php artisan test`, `go test ./...`, `go vet ./...` and `npm test` in the appropriate directories.

MySQL/Docker deployment and a real FTPS endpoint have **not** been exercised in this environment. Native screen capture, foreground detection, tray behavior and DPAPI need an interactive Windows smoke test; sandboxed automation cannot validate those desktop integrations fully. Browser URL detection is best effort and depends on browser accessibility support; it is off by default. Secure/locked desktops and protected windows may not be capturable. This is foreground sampling, not a list of all running apps, idle detection, keystroke logging or a productivity score.

Screenshots occur once per interval while the agent is awake, signed in and unpaused; sleep, failed captures, a full queue or network policy changes can create gaps. Administrator revocation takes effect when the agent next contacts the server (normally within 30 seconds); offline agents follow their last policy until token expiry. The tray does not prevent users from terminating their own process. Retention is an application setting, not a compliance certification.

The repository includes working application source and deployment configuration. Production operation still requires your server, TLS, database credentials, storage configuration and Windows rollout.

## Review fixes

See [REVIEW-RESOLUTION.md](REVIEW-RESOLUTION.md) for verified findings, regression tests and deferred suggestions. Invalid queue records are quarantined. Permanently rejected uploads and uploads failing 100 attempts stop retrying but remain on disk within the queue budget until retention expiry. Large originals above 16 million pixels use the gallery original-image fallback instead of a generated thumbnail.

## Publish the source on GitHub

Extract the GitHub source ZIP and open a terminal in its `activity-platform` directory. Create an empty repository in your GitHub account, then run:

```powershell
git init
git add .
git status --short
git commit -m "Initial Activity Platform source release"
git branch -M main
git remote add origin https://github.com/YOUR_USERNAME/YOUR_REPOSITORY.git
git push -u origin main
```

Replace the example repository URL with your own. Review the staged files before committing. The included `.gitignore` excludes `.env` files, private keys, local data, dependencies and executables. Commit `.env.example`, `composer.lock` and `web/package-lock.json`. Do not copy your production environment or employee records into the repository.

No project-wide license has been selected for this application. Choose your intended license and add a root `LICENSE` before inviting public reuse; dependency licenses and Laravel skeleton metadata do not automatically license the entire project.

To generate a new source-only ZIP from PowerShell 7:

```powershell
./scripts/package.ps1 -SourceOnly
```

To package a built distribution including the executable, first build the frontend and agent, then run `./scripts/package.ps1` without the switch. Upload binaries as GitHub Release assets rather than committing them. The packaging command prints the archive's SHA-256 checksum. This package does not create or publish a GitHub repository automatically.

## Common installation problems

- **404 in Herd:** link the `server` directory, not the project root or `web` directory.
- **Database connection refused / missing driver:** start MySQL, use its actual port and credentials, and enable PDO MySQL in the selected PHP version.
- **Missing session/cache tables:** run `artisan migrate --seed` after configuring the database.
- **419 after changing domains:** set APP_URL correctly, keep SESSION_DOMAIN unset/null, clear configuration, and sign in again on the HTTPS domain.
- **No gallery thumbnails:** ensure GD and the queue worker are running; inspect `artisan queue:failed` and `server/storage/logs/laravel.log`.
- **Frontend changes are missing:** run `node scripts/build-web.mjs`; rebuild the Go executable to update its embedded UI.
- **Agent cannot connect:** verify `server_url`, HTTPS trust and server availability. The localhost agent page and the Laravel server are different addresses.
- **Screenshots missing:** check employee login, administrator policy/device pause, queue status and the interactive Windows session. See known limits above.

# Review resolution

This pass addresses the attached review's bug findings. The 80 suggested enhancements are a future roadmap, not features implemented by this patch.

## Changes

- **Queue recovery (#5):** invalid manifests and missing payload records move to `data/quarantine`; healthy records continue loading. Payload paths are derived from validated filenames, never corrupt JSON. Quarantined files count toward the queue's storage budget and expire under offline retention.
- **Permanent failures (#4):** HTTP 400, 413, 415 and 422 mark records as failed. Other failures stop automatic retries after 100 attempts. Failed manifests and payloads remain in the bounded queue until retention expires. The local UI shows their count. The manifests' `failure` fields and diagnostic logs explain the state; no automatic replay of failed records is provided.
- **Scheduling (#2):** explicit fixed-window advancement skips elapsed sleep windows. A fresh random target is chosen from the remaining part of the current window, never from an already elapsed part. A consumed window is not replayed. This remains one attempted capture per available window, with documented gaps for sleep, cancellation and failures.
- **Thumbnail concurrency (#3):** each attempt writes a unique file, then publishes it with a conditional `WHERE thumbnail_path IS NULL` update. A losing attempt deletes only its own file. Retention reloads the screenshot under a row lock before deletion so it includes newly published thumbnails.
- **Thumbnail memory (#24):** inspect dimensions before GD decoding; inputs above 16 million pixels retain their original image without generating a thumbnail. The existing gallery fallback displays the original. Ingestion still permits multi-monitor originals up to 64 million pixels / 20 MB.
- **Literal search (#10):** application/title filters escape LIKE wildcards with an explicit escape character, using bound parameters on both MySQL and SQLite.
- **Intranet URLs (#11):** explicitly schemed single-label HTTP(S) hosts are accepted; ambiguous bare search words remain rejected.
- **Policy reads (#14–17):** hydrate defaults only on creation and reuse one policy snapshot per operation. No persistent cache was added, so administration changes do not wait for cache expiry.
- **Mixed DPI (#18):** request per-monitor V2 awareness for the capture process/thread, with a legacy fallback. Live mixed-DPI display testing remains necessary.
- **PNG validation:** explicitly check the PNG signature in addition to file type and dimension validation.
- **Queue accounting (#20):** document and reserve manifest growth space for retry/failure metadata.

## Findings that did not reproduce

- **Windows replacement (#1, #6):** the installed Go standard library implements `os.Rename` with `MoveFileEx(..., MOVEFILE_REPLACE_EXISTING)`. A Windows regression test overwrites the same file three times and verifies its contents. Do not delete the old file before replacement: that would introduce an unnecessary data-loss window. This confirms replacement behavior, not a general Windows filesystem atomicity guarantee. `loadIdentity` also propagates write errors; it does not silently ignore them.
- **Token expiry (#12):** installed Sanctum checks `expires_at` independently of its global `expiration` option in `vendor/laravel/sanctum/src/Guard.php::isValidAccessToken`. A regression test sets the global option to null and verifies that an expired device token receives HTTP 401.
- **FTPS deletion (#9):** curl supports `--quote -DELE name` after a successful transfer. Listing the parent directory then deleting a relative filename is valid. See [curl --quote documentation](https://curl.se/docs/manpage.html#-Q). Real FTPS endpoint integration is still unverified; remote deletion failures remain visible and retain the database record for retry.
- **Capture cancellation (#7):** both cancellation branches already remove the staged payload before returning.
- **Filename slicing (#19), random seeding (#21), auth session regeneration (#13), and retention test (#23):** the review itself correctly concludes these are not bugs.
- **Original-app test/global settings references (#22, #28, #29):** do not apply to this project.
- **Old timestamps (#26):** retention is based on capture time, so older captures expire sooner, not later. Already-expired events are acknowledged and discarded.
- **Enrollment attribution (#27):** employee ID and IP were already recorded in metadata. The audit actor remains system for that pre-session operation.
- **Host matching (#30):** exact loopback Host matching is intentional; use the address printed by the agent.

## Deliberate limits and deferred work

Retention of screenshots, activity and audit is independent (#8). A failed remote image deletion does not block deletion of expired unrelated activity/audit. A database rollback cannot restore files already deleted from FTPS; partial storage cleanup may require operator reconciliation. Errors return command failure and keep the screenshot record.

CSV exports remain streamed with a preflight count and a 100,000-row / 31-day limit (#25). Cursor pagination, full-text search, precomputed counters and other scale optimizations need workload measurements. Changing pagination semantics or silently truncating CSV output was not part of this bug pass.

This is a **single-organization application with roles**, not a multi-tenant platform. Dashboard authentication uses Laravel web sessions and CSRF; device authentication uses Sanctum tokens. Audit logging covers the implemented review/management actions, not literally every database read.

No new legal compliance certification, DPA, geofence, off-hours monitoring, blur filter, SSO, metrics platform, third-party telemetry service or device fleet installer was added. Existing MySQL/Docker, FTPS and interactive native-Windows validation limitations still apply.

## Verification

- Go: 12 passing tests, including Windows replacement, retry persistence, corrupted queue isolation, terminal failures, window advancement and intranet URL sanitization.
- Laravel: 17 passing tests / 73 assertions, including server-enforced token expiry, literal search, interleaved thumbnail publication and pre-decode dimension limits.
- Frontend: 2 utility tests; production bundle rebuilt and embedded in the rebuilt Windows executable.
- Go vet and PHP Pint run before packaging.

The concurrency test deliberately interleaves two thumbnail attempts; it does not replace a multi-process MySQL load test. FTPS syntax validation is based on curl's contract, not a live FTPS integration test.

<script setup>
import { onMounted, onUnmounted, reactive, ref } from 'vue'
import { api, errorMessage, localTime } from './api'
const clock = ref(new Date().toLocaleString()); let clockTimer
const state = ref(null), error = ref(''), busy = ref(false), accepted = ref(false)
const credentials = reactive({email:'',password:''}); let timer
async function refresh(){try{state.value=(await api.get('/local/status')).data}catch(err){error.value='Cannot reach the local agent. '+errorMessage(err)}}
async function login(){busy.value=true;error.value='';try{await api.post('/local/login',{...credentials,notice_accepted:accepted.value});credentials.password='';await refresh()}catch(err){error.value=errorMessage(err)}finally{busy.value=false}}
async function logout(){busy.value=true;try{await api.post('/local/logout');await refresh()}catch(err){error.value=errorMessage(err)}finally{busy.value=false}}

import axios from 'axios'

export const api = axios.create({
  baseURL: '/',
  withCredentials: true,
  withXSRFToken: true,
  headers: { Accept: 'application/json' },
  timeout: 30000,
})

export function errorMessage(error) {
  const data = error.response?.data
  return Object.values(data?.errors ?? {}).flat().join(' ') || data?.message || error.message || 'The request failed.'
}

export function localTime(value) {
  return value ? new Date(value).toLocaleString(undefined, { dateStyle: 'medium', timeStyle: 'short' }) : 'Never'
}

export function filterParams(filters) {
  return Object.fromEntries(Object.entries(filters).filter(([, value]) => value !== '' && value != null))
}

<laravel-boost-guidelines>
# Laravel Application

This repository contains a Laravel application. Complete the following setup before working on the user's request.

## Prerequisites

Verify that PHP and Composer are available:

```sh
php -v
composer -V
```

If either command is unavailable, detect the user's operating system and install the prerequisites with the appropriate command:

macOS:

```sh
/bin/bash -c "$(curl -fsSL https://php.new/install/mac/8.5)"
```

Windows PowerShell:

```powershell
Set-ExecutionPolicy Bypass -Scope Process -Force; [System.Net.ServicePointManager]::SecurityProtocol = [System.Net.ServicePointManager]::SecurityProtocol -bor 3072; iex ((New-Object System.Net.WebClient).DownloadString('https://php.new/install/windows/8.5'))
```

Linux:

```sh
/bin/bash -c "$(curl -fsSL https://php.new/install/linux/8.5)"
```

After installation, ask the user to restart their terminal. If the agent needs the restarted shell to continue, ask the user to reopen their terminal and rerun their original prompt.

## Agent Setup

Install Laravel Boost from the application root before making application changes:

```sh
composer require laravel/boost --dev
php artisan boost:install
```

Boost replaces these bootstrap instructions with guidelines tailored to the application. After installation, read `AGENTS.md` again and continue with the user's original request using the generated guidelines.
</laravel-boost-guidelines>

<laravel-boost-guidelines>
=== foundation rules ===

# Laravel Boost Guidelines

The Laravel Boost guidelines are specifically curated by Laravel maintainers for this application. These guidelines should be followed closely to ensure the best experience when building Laravel applications.

## Foundational Context

This application is a Laravel application running on PHP 8.4. You are an expert with the Laravel ecosystem. Always use the APIs that match the installed major version of each package — do not assume a version.

Before relying on a package's API, confirm its installed version:
- PHP packages: run `composer show --direct` to list direct dependencies with versions, or `composer show <vendor/package>` for a single package.
- JS packages: check `package.json` for the installed versions.

## Conventions

- You must follow all existing code conventions used in this application. When creating or editing a file, check sibling files for the correct structure, approach, and naming.
- Use descriptive names for variables and methods. For example, `isRegisteredForDiscounts`, not `discount()`.
- Check for existing components to reuse before writing a new one.

## Verification Scripts

- Do not create verification scripts or tinker when tests cover that functionality and prove they work. Unit and feature tests are more important.

## Application Structure & Architecture

- Stick to existing directory structure; don't create new base folders without approval.
- Do not change the application's dependencies without approval.

## Frontend Bundling

- If the user doesn't see a frontend change reflected in the UI, it could mean they need to run `npm run build`, `npm run dev`, or `composer run dev`. Ask them.

## Documentation Files

- You must only create documentation files if explicitly requested by the user.

## Replies

- Be concise in your explanations - focus on what's important rather than explaining obvious details.

=== boost rules ===

# Laravel Boost

## Project Rules

- This project contains committed, area-grouped rules in `.ai/rules` when that directory exists (settled decisions, non-obvious traps, standing constraints). Framework and package guidelines that only apply to specific paths (testing, frontend, components) also live there, under `.ai/rules/boost` — this is not just recorded decisions, it is load-bearing guidance you have not seen inline. Before you enter plan mode or create/edit any file, you MUST first: open @.ai/rules/index.md (it maps file globs to rule files), read every rule file whose globs cover the path(s) in scope, and run `grep -rin 'keyword' .ai/rules` to catch what a path match alone misses. Do not write code until you have read and are following every matching rule. If `.ai/rules` does not exist, continue without it.

## Artisan

- Run Artisan commands directly via the command line (e.g., `php artisan route:list`). Use `php artisan list` to discover available commands and `php artisan [command] --help` to check parameters.
- Inspect routes with `php artisan route:list`. Filter with: `--method=GET`, `--name=users`, `--path=api`, `--except-vendor`, `--only-vendor`.
- Read configuration values using dot notation: `php artisan config:show app.name`, `php artisan config:show database.default`. Or read config files directly from the `config/` directory.

## Tinker

- Execute PHP in app context for debugging and testing code. Do not create models without user approval, prefer tests with factories instead. Prefer existing Artisan commands over custom tinker code.
- Always use single quotes to prevent shell expansion: `php artisan tinker --execute 'Your::code();'`
  - Double quotes for PHP strings inside: `php artisan tinker --execute 'User::where("active", true)->count();'`

=== php rules ===

# PHP

- Always use curly braces for control structures, even for single-line bodies.
- Use PHP 8 constructor property promotion: `public function __construct(public GitHub $github) { }`. Do not leave empty zero-parameter `__construct()` methods unless the constructor is private.
- Use explicit return type declarations and type hints for all method parameters: `function isAccessible(User $user, ?string $path = null): bool`
- Use TitleCase for Enum keys: `FavoritePerson`, `BestLake`, `Monthly`.
- Prefer PHPDoc blocks over inline comments. Only add inline comments for exceptionally complex logic.
- Use array shape type definitions in PHPDoc blocks.

=== deployments rules ===

# Deployment

- Laravel can be deployed using [Laravel Cloud](https://cloud.laravel.com/), which is the fastest way to deploy and scale production Laravel applications.
- Activate the `deploying-to-cloud` skill whenever deploying to Laravel Cloud, configuring Cloud environments or resources, using the Cloud CLI, or troubleshooting Cloud deployments.

=== laravel/core rules ===

# Do Things the Laravel Way

- Use `php artisan make:` commands to create new files (i.e. migrations, controllers, models, etc.). You can list available Artisan commands using `php artisan list` and check their parameters with `php artisan [command] --help`.
- If you're creating a generic PHP class, use `php artisan make:class`.
- Pass `--no-interaction` to all Artisan commands to ensure they work without user input. You should also pass the correct `--options` to ensure correct behavior.

### Model Creation

- When creating new models, create useful factories and seeders for them too. Ask the user if they need any other things, using `php artisan make:model --help` to check the available options.

## APIs & Eloquent Resources

- For APIs, default to using Eloquent API Resources and API versioning unless existing API routes do not, then you should follow existing application convention.

## URL Generation

- When generating links to other pages, prefer named routes and the `route()` function.

## Testing

- When creating models for tests, use the factories for the models. Check if the factory has custom states that can be used before manually setting up the model.
- Faker: Use methods such as `$this->faker->word()` or `fake()->randomDigit()`. Follow existing conventions whether to use `$this->faker` or `fake()`.
- When creating tests, make use of `php artisan make:test [options] {name}` to create a feature test, and pass `--unit` to create a unit test. Most tests should be feature tests.

## Vite Error

- If you receive an "Illuminate\Foundation\ViteException: Unable to locate file in Vite manifest" error, you can run `npm run build` or ask the user to run `npm run dev` or `composer run dev`.

=== pint/core rules ===

# Laravel Pint Code Formatter

- If you have modified any PHP files, you must run `vendor/bin/pint --dirty --format agent` before finalizing changes to ensure your code matches the project's expected style.
- Do not run `vendor/bin/pint --test --format agent`, simply run `vendor/bin/pint --format agent` to fix any formatting issues.

=== phpunit/core rules ===

# PHPUnit

- This project uses PHPUnit. Create tests with `php artisan make:test --phpunit {name}`.
- Do not include the test suite directory in `{name}`. Use `SomeFeatureTest`, not `Feature/SomeFeatureTest`.
- Read the `testing-best-practices` skill for guidance on coverage, naming, structure, dependency isolation, and review.

## Running Tests

- Run the narrowest set of tests that covers the change. Pass a file path or `--filter=testName` to `php artisan test --compact`.
- Rerun a test after each change to it.
- Run `vendor/bin/phpunit` to call the test runner directly. It accepts the same file path and `--filter=testName` arguments.

</laravel-boost-guidelines>

## About Laravel

Laravel is a web application framework with expressive, elegant syntax. We believe development must be an enjoyable and creative experience to be truly fulfilling. Laravel takes the pain out of development by easing common tasks used in many web projects, such as:

- [Simple, fast routing engine](https://laravel.com/docs/routing).
- [Powerful dependency injection container](https://laravel.com/docs/container).
- Multiple back-ends for [session](https://laravel.com/docs/session) and [cache](https://laravel.com/docs/cache) storage.
- Expressive, intuitive [database ORM](https://laravel.com/docs/eloquent).
- Database agnostic [schema migrations](https://laravel.com/docs/migrations).
- [Robust background job processing](https://laravel.com/docs/queues).
- [Real-time event broadcasting](https://laravel.com/docs/broadcasting).

Laravel is accessible, powerful, and provides tools required for large, robust applications.

## Learning Laravel

Laravel has the most extensive and thorough [documentation](https://laravel.com/docs) and video tutorial library of all modern web application frameworks, making it a breeze to get started with the framework.

In addition, [Laracasts](https://laracasts.com) contains thousands of video tutorials on a range of topics including Laravel, modern PHP, unit testing, and JavaScript. Boost your skills by digging into our comprehensive video library.

You can also watch bite-sized lessons with real-world projects on [Laravel Learn](https://laravel.com/learn), where you will be guided through building a Laravel application from scratch while learning PHP fundamentals.

## Agentic Development

Laravel's predictable structure and conventions make it ideal for AI coding agents like Claude Code, Cursor, and GitHub Copilot. Install [Laravel Boost](https://laravel.com/docs/ai) to supercharge your AI workflow:

```bash
composer require laravel/boost --dev

php artisan boost:install
```

Boost provides your agent 15+ tools and skills that help agents build Laravel applications while following best practices.

## Contributing

Thank you for considering contributing to the Laravel framework! The contribution guide can be found in the [Laravel documentation](https://laravel.com/docs/contributions).

## Code of Conduct

In order to ensure that the Laravel community is welcoming to all, please review and abide by the [Code of Conduct](https://laravel.com/docs/contributions#code-of-conduct).

## Security Vulnerabilities

If you discover a security vulnerability within Laravel, please send an e-mail to Taylor Otwell via [taylor@laravel.com](mailto:taylor@laravel.com). All security vulnerabilities will be promptly addressed.

## License

The Laravel framework is open-sourced software licensed under the [MIT license](https://opensource.org/licenses/MIT).

 FILE: server\tests\Feature\TrackerTest.php [223 lines | 11.5 KB | php]

<?php

namespace Tests\Feature;

use App\Jobs\GenerateThumbnail;
use App\Models\ActivityLog;
use App\Models\AuditLog;
use App\Models\Device;
use App\Models\MonitoringPolicy;
use App\Models\Screenshot;
use App\Models\User;
use App\Services\Vault;
use Illuminate\Foundation\Testing\RefreshDatabase;
use Illuminate\Http\UploadedFile;
use Illuminate\Support\Facades\Queue;
use Illuminate\Support\Facades\Storage;
use Illuminate\Support\Str;
use Laravel\Sanctum\PersonalAccessToken;
use Tests\TestCase;

class TrackerTest extends TestCase
{
    use RefreshDatabase;

    protected function setUp(): void
    {
        parent::setUp();
        Storage::fake('local');
        config(['tracker.storage' => 'local']);
        MonitoringPolicy::current();
    }

    private function enroll(?User $user = null): array
    {
        $user ??= User::factory()->create(['role' => 'employee']);

        return $this->postJson('/api/agent/login', ['email' => $user->email, 'password' => 'password', 'device_identifier' => (string) Str::uuid(), 'device_name' => 'Test PC', 'os' => 'windows', 'notice_accepted' => true])->assertOk()->json();
    }

    public function test_expired_device_token_is_rejected_without_global_expiration(): void
    {
        config(['sanctum.expiration' => null]);
        $login = $this->enroll();
        $token = PersonalAccessToken::findToken($login['token']);
        $token->update(['expires_at' => now()->subMinute()]);
        $this->withToken($login['token'])->postJson('/api/agent/heartbeat')->assertUnauthorized();
    }

    public function test_search_treats_percent_and_underscore_as_literal_characters(): void
    {
        ActivityLog::factory()->create(['window_title' => '100%_done!', 'app_name' => 'app_100%.exe']);
        ActivityLog::factory()->create(['window_title' => '100XXdone!', 'app_name' => 'appX100YY.exe']);
        $reviewer = User::factory()->create(['role' => 'reviewer']);
        $this->actingAs($reviewer)->getJson('/api/admin/activity?'.http_build_query(['search' => '%_', 'app' => '_100%']))->assertOk()->assertJsonCount(1, 'data')->assertJsonPath('data.0.window_title', '100%_done!');
    }

    public function test_competing_thumbnail_jobs_publish_one_file_and_remove_only_the_loser(): void
    {
        $shot = Screenshot::factory()->create();
        $source = UploadedFile::fake()->image('source.png', 20, 20);
        $vault = app(Vault::class);
        $vault->put($shot->path, file_get_contents($source->getRealPath()));
        $loserPath = null;
        $competingVault = \Mockery::mock(Vault::class)->makePartial();
        $competingVault->shouldReceive('put')->once()->andReturnUsing(function (string $path, string $bytes, ?string $driver) use ($vault, $shot, &$loserPath): void {
            $loserPath = $path;
            $vault->put($path, $bytes, $driver);
            (new GenerateThumbnail($shot->id))->handle($vault);
        });
        (new GenerateThumbnail($shot->id))->handle($competingVault);
        $winnerPath = $shot->fresh()->thumbnail_path;
        $this->assertNotNull($winnerPath);
        $this->assertNotSame($loserPath, $winnerPath);
        Storage::disk('local')->assertExists('tracker/'.$winnerPath);
        Storage::disk('local')->assertMissing('tracker/'.$loserPath);
    }

    public function test_large_thumbnail_input_is_skipped_before_gd_decode(): void
    {
        $shot = Screenshot::factory()->create();
        $source = UploadedFile::fake()->image('source.png', 2, 2);
        $bytes = file_get_contents($source->getRealPath());
        $bytes = substr_replace($bytes, pack('NN', 5000, 5000), 16, 8);
        $vault = app(Vault::class);
        $vault->put($shot->path, $bytes);
        (new GenerateThumbnail($shot->id))->handle($vault);
        $this->assertNull($shot->fresh()->thumbnail_path);
        Storage::disk('local')->assertExists('tracker/'.$shot->path);
    }

    public function test_admin_login_roles_and_disabled_accounts(): void
    {
        $admin = User::factory()->create(['role' => 'super_admin']);
        $this->postJson('/api/admin/login', ['email' => $admin->email, 'password' => 'bad'])->assertUnprocessable();
        $this->postJson('/api/admin/login', ['email' => $admin->email, 'password' => 'password'])->assertOk()->assertJsonPath('user.role', 'super_admin');
        $this->getJson('/api/admin/users')->assertOk();
        $this->postJson('/api/admin/logout')->assertOk();
        $employee = User::factory()->create();
        $this->postJson('/api/admin/login', ['email' => $employee->email, 'password' => 'password'])->assertUnprocessable();
        $this->getJson('/api/admin/users')->assertUnauthorized();
        $admin->update(['enabled' => false]);
        $this->postJson('/api/admin/login', ['email' => $admin->email, 'password' => 'password'])->assertUnprocessable();
    }

    public function test_reviewer_can_review_but_cannot_manage(): void
    {
        $reviewer = User::factory()->create(['role' => 'reviewer']);
        $this->actingAs($reviewer)->getJson('/api/admin/screenshots')->assertOk();
        $this->getJson('/api/admin/users')->assertForbidden();
        $this->putJson('/api/admin/policy', [])->assertForbidden();
        $this->getJson('/api/admin/audit')->assertForbidden();
    }

    public function test_device_requires_notice_and_cannot_be_reassigned(): void
    {
        $user = User::factory()->create();
        $identifier = (string) Str::uuid();
        $body = ['email' => $user->email, 'password' => 'password', 'device_identifier' => $identifier, 'device_name' => 'PC', 'os' => 'windows', 'notice_accepted' => false];
        $this->postJson('/api/agent/login', $body)->assertUnprocessable();
        $this->postJson('/api/agent/login', [...$body, 'notice_accepted' => true])->assertOk();
        $other = User::factory()->create();
        $this->postJson('/api/agent/login', [...$body, 'email' => $other->email, 'notice_accepted' => true])->assertForbidden();
        $this->assertDatabaseCount('devices', 1);
    }

    public function test_device_token_cannot_access_admin_endpoints_and_disable_revokes_it(): void
    {
        $session = $this->enroll();
        $this->withToken($session['token'])->postJson('/api/agent/heartbeat')->assertOk();
        $this->getJson('/api/admin/users')->assertUnauthorized();
        Device::find($session['device']['id'])->update(['disabled_at' => now()]);
        $this->postJson('/api/agent/heartbeat')->assertForbidden();
    }

    public function test_screenshot_upload_is_private_idempotent_and_thumbnail_is_generated(): void
    {
        Queue::fake();
        $session = $this->enroll();
        $id = (string) Str::uuid();
        $file = UploadedFile::fake()->image('screen.png', 1200, 700);
        $bytes = file_get_contents($file->getRealPath());
        $body = ['event_id' => $id, 'captured_at' => now()->toIso8601String(), 'file' => $file, 'app_name' => 'editor.exe'];
        $response = $this->withToken($session['token'])->postJson('/api/agent/screenshots', $body)->assertCreated()->assertJsonPath('accepted', true);
        $shot = Screenshot::find($response->json('id'));
        Storage::disk('local')->assertExists('tracker/'.$shot->path);
        $body['file'] = UploadedFile::fake()->createWithContent('again.png', $bytes);
        $this->postJson('/api/agent/screenshots', $body)->assertOk();
        $this->assertDatabaseCount('screenshots', 1);
        Queue::assertPushed(GenerateThumbnail::class, 1);
        (new GenerateThumbnail($shot->id))->handle(app(Vault::class));
        $this->assertNotNull($shot->fresh()->thumbnail_path);
        $this->getJson('/api/admin/screenshots/'.$shot->id.'/file')->assertUnauthorized();
    }

    public function test_gallery_file_access_is_audited(): void
    {
        $shot = Screenshot::factory()->create();
        app(Vault::class)->put($shot->path, 'test-image');
        $reviewer = User::factory()->create(['role' => 'reviewer']);
        $this->actingAs($reviewer)->get('/api/admin/screenshots/'.$shot->id.'/file')->assertOk()->assertHeader('Content-Type', 'image/png');
        $this->assertDatabaseHas('audit_logs', ['actor_id' => $reviewer->id, 'action' => 'screenshot.viewed', 'subject_id' => $shot->id]);
    }

    public function test_activity_batch_is_idempotent_and_strips_url_secrets(): void
    {
        MonitoringPolicy::current()->update(['browser_urls' => true]);
        $session = $this->enroll();
        $event = ['event_id' => (string) Str::uuid(), 'captured_at' => now()->toIso8601String(), 'app_name' => 'chrome.exe', 'window_title' => 'Report', 'url' => 'https://user:secret@example.com/report?token=secret#anchor'];
        $this->withToken($session['token'])->postJson('/api/agent/activity', ['events' => [$event]])->assertOk()->assertJsonPath('accepted_ids.0', $event['event_id']);
        $this->postJson('/api/agent/activity', ['events' => [$event]])->assertOk();
        $this->assertDatabaseCount('activity_logs', 1);
        $this->assertDatabaseHas('activity_logs', ['url' => 'https://example.com/report']);
    }

    public function test_admin_pause_prevents_new_ingestion(): void
    {
        $session = $this->enroll();
        Device::find($session['device']['id'])->update(['paused' => true]);
        $this->withToken($session['token'])->postJson('/api/agent/heartbeat')->assertOk()->assertJsonPath('policy.monitoring_enabled', false);
        $event = ['event_id' => (string) Str::uuid(), 'captured_at' => now()->toIso8601String(), 'app_name' => 'test.exe'];
        $this->postJson('/api/agent/activity', ['events' => [$event]])->assertStatus(409);
        $this->assertDatabaseCount('activity_logs', 0);
    }

    public function test_user_disable_revokes_devices_and_preserves_records(): void
    {
        $session = $this->enroll();
        $admin = User::factory()->create(['role' => 'super_admin']);
        $this->actingAs($admin)->patchJson('/api/admin/users/'.$session['user']['id'], ['enabled' => false])->assertOk();
        $device = Device::find($session['device']['id']);
        $this->assertNotNull($device->disabled_at);
        $this->assertNull($device->token_id);
        $this->assertDatabaseCount('personal_access_tokens', 0);
        $this->patchJson('/api/admin/users/'.$admin->id, ['enabled' => false])->assertUnprocessable();
    }

    public function test_csv_export_neutralizes_spreadsheet_formulas_and_is_audited(): void
    {
        ActivityLog::factory()->create(['window_title' => '=1+1']);
        $reviewer = User::factory()->create(['role' => 'reviewer']);
        $response = $this->actingAs($reviewer)->get('/api/admin/activity/export');
        $response->assertOk();
        $this->assertStringContainsString("'=1+1", $response->streamedContent());
        $this->assertDatabaseHas('audit_logs', ['action' => 'activity.exported', 'actor_id' => $reviewer->id]);
    }

    public function test_retention_removes_expired_files_and_keeps_recent_data(): void
    {
        $old = Screenshot::factory()->create(['captured_at' => now()->subDays(40)]);
        app(Vault::class)->put($old->path, 'old screenshot');
        $recent = Screenshot::factory()->create();
        app(Vault::class)->put($recent->path, 'recent screenshot');
        ActivityLog::factory()->create(['captured_at' => now()->subDays(40)]);
        AuditLog::factory()->create(['created_at' => now()->subDays(400)]);
        $this->artisan('tracker:prune')->assertSuccessful();
        Storage::disk('local')->assertMissing('tracker/'.$old->path);
        Storage::disk('local')->assertExists('tracker/'.$recent->path);
        $this->assertDatabaseCount('screenshots', 1);
        $this->assertDatabaseCount('activity_logs', 0);
        $this->assertDatabaseCount('audit_logs', 0);
    }
}

<?php

namespace Database\Seeders;

use App\Jobs\GenerateThumbnail;
use App\Models\ActivityLog;
use App\Models\Device;
use App\Models\MonitoringPolicy;
use App\Models\Screenshot;
use App\Models\User;
use App\Services\Vault;
use Illuminate\Database\Seeder;
use Illuminate\Support\Str;

class DemoSeeder extends Seeder
{
    /**
     * Run the database seeds.
     */
    public function run(): void
    {
        if (! app()->environment(['local', 'testing']) || config('tracker.storage') !== 'local') {
            throw new \RuntimeException('Demo data is allowed only in local/testing with local storage.');
        }
        MonitoringPolicy::current();
        foreach (['admin' => 'super_admin', 'reviewer' => 'reviewer', 'employee' => 'employee'] as $name => $role) {
            User::firstOrCreate(['email' => $name.'@example.test'], ['name' => ucfirst($name).' Demo', 'password' => 'LocalDemo!2026', 'role' => $role]);
        }
        $employee = User::where('email', 'employee@example.test')->firstOrFail();
        $device = Device::firstOrCreate(['device_identifier' => '11111111-1111-4111-8111-111111111111'], ['user_id' => $employee->id, 'name' => 'Demo workstation', 'os' => 'Windows', 'paused' => true, 'notice_version' => 1, 'notice_accepted_at' => now()]);
        if (Screenshot::where('device_id', $device->id)->exists()) {
            return;
        }
        $vault = app(Vault::class);
        foreach (['Code editor', 'Browser', 'Spreadsheet'] as $index => $application) {
            $image = imagecreatetruecolor(1000, 625);
            imagefill($image, 0, 0, imagecolorallocate($image, 235, 243, 241));
            $ink = imagecolorallocate($image, 28, 57, 67);
            imagestring($image, 5, 50, 55, 'SYNTHETIC DEMO - '.$application, $ink);
            imagestring($image, 4, 50, 100, 'This image contains no captured desktop data.', $ink);
            for ($row = 0; $row < 6; $row++) {
                imagefilledrectangle($image, 50, 160 + $row * 55, 900 - $row * 35, 185 + $row * 55, imagecolorallocate($image, 175 + $row * 8, 201 + $row * 5, 193 + $row * 5));
            }
            ob_start();
            imagepng($image);
            $bytes = ob_get_clean();
            imagedestroy($image);
            $event = (string) Str::uuid();
            $path = 'screenshots/'.$device->id.'/'.$event.'.png';
            $vault->put($path, $bytes);
            $shot = Screenshot::create(['device_id' => $device->id, 'event_id' => $event, 'captured_at' => now()->subMinutes($index * 3), 'path' => $path, 'storage' => 'local', 'sha256' => hash('sha256', $bytes), 'bytes' => strlen($bytes), 'app_name' => $application, 'window_title' => 'Synthetic demonstration']);
            GenerateThumbnail::dispatchSync($shot->id);
            ActivityLog::create(['device_id' => $device->id, 'event_id' => (string) Str::uuid(), 'captured_at' => $shot->captured_at, 'app_name' => $application, 'window_title' => 'Synthetic demonstration', 'created_at' => now()]);
        }
    }
}

<?php

namespace Database\Factories;

use App\Models\User;
use Illuminate\Database\Eloquent\Factories\Factory;
use Illuminate\Support\Facades\Hash;
use Illuminate\Support\Str;

/**
 * @extends Factory<User>
 */
class UserFactory extends Factory
{
    /**
     * The current password being used by the factory.
     */
    protected static ?string $password;

    /**
     * Define the model's default state.
     *
     * @return array<string, mixed>
     */
    public function definition(): array
    {
        return [
            'name' => fake()->name(),
            'email' => fake()->unique()->safeEmail(),
            'email_verified_at' => now(),
            'password' => static::$password ??= Hash::make('password'),
            'remember_token' => Str::random(10),
        ];
    }

    /**
     * Indicate that the model's email address should be unverified.
     */
    public function unverified(): static
    {
        return $this->state(fn (array $attributes) => [
            'email_verified_at' => null,
        ]);
    }
}

 FILE: server\app\Services\Vault.php [103 lines | 3.8 KB | php]
────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

<?php

namespace App\Services;

use Illuminate\Support\Facades\Storage;
use Illuminate\Support\Str;
use RuntimeException;
use Symfony\Component\Process\Process;

class Vault
{
    public function put(string $path, string $bytes, ?string $driver = null): void
    {
        $driver ??= config('tracker.storage');
        $this->validatePath($path);
        if ($driver === 'local') {
            if (! Storage::disk('local')->put('tracker/'.$path, $bytes)) {
                throw new RuntimeException('Private storage write failed.');
            }

            return;
        }
        $temporary = tempnam(sys_get_temp_dir(), 'tracker-upload-');
        try {
            if (file_put_contents($temporary, $bytes) === false) {
                throw new RuntimeException('Cannot stage storage upload.');
            }
            $this->ftp($path, ['--ftp-create-dirs', '--upload-file', $temporary]);
        } finally {
            if (is_file($temporary)) {
                unlink($temporary);
            }
        }
    }

    public function get(string $path, ?string $driver = null): string
    {
        $this->validatePath($path);
        if (($driver ?? config('tracker.storage')) === 'local') {
            $bytes = Storage::disk('local')->get('tracker/'.$path);
            if ($bytes === null) {
                throw new RuntimeException('Stored file is unavailable.');
            }

            return $bytes;
        }

        return $this->ftp($path, []);
    }

    public function delete(string $path, ?string $driver = null): void
    {
        $this->validatePath($path);
        if (($driver ?? config('tracker.storage')) === 'local') {
            if (! Storage::disk('local')->delete('tracker/'.$path)) {
                throw new RuntimeException('Storage delete failed.');
            }

            return;
        }
        $this->ftp(dirname($path).'/', ['--list-only', '--quote', '-DELE '.basename($path)]);
    }

    public function check(): void
    {
        $path = 'checks/'.Str::uuid().'.txt';
        $contents = 'activity-storage-check';
        $this->put($path, $contents);
        try {
            if ($this->get($path) !== $contents) {
                throw new RuntimeException('Storage verification failed.');
            }
        } finally {
            $this->delete($path);
        }
    }

    private function validatePath(string $path): void
    {
        if (! preg_match('~^[A-Za-z0-9_./-]+$~', $path) || str_contains($path, '..') || str_starts_with($path, '/')) {
            throw new RuntimeException('Invalid storage path.');
        }
    }

    private function ftp(string $path, array $extra): string
    {
        $base = config('tracker.ftps_url');
        $parts = parse_url($base ?? '');
        if (! $parts || ! in_array($parts['scheme'] ?? '', ['ftp', 'ftps'], true) || empty($parts['host']) || isset($parts['user']) || isset($parts['query']) || isset($parts['fragment'])) {
            throw new RuntimeException('Configure a valid FTPS folder URL on the server.');
        }
        $quote = static fn (string $value): string => '"'.str_replace(['\\', '"', "\n", "\r"], ['\\\\', '\"', '\n', '\r'], $value).'"';
        $config = 'url = '.$quote(rtrim($base, '/').'/'.$path)."\n".'user = '.$quote(config('tracker.ftps_username').':'.config('tracker.ftps_password'))."\n";
        $process = new Process([config('tracker.curl_binary'), '--disable', '--config', '-', '--silent', '--show-error', '--fail', '--globoff', '--ssl-reqd', '--connect-timeout', '10', '--max-time', '40', ...$extra], null, null, $config, 45);
        $process->run();
        if (! $process->isSuccessful()) {
            throw new RuntimeException('FTPS storage request failed. Check server credentials, certificates, folder permissions and connectivity.');
        }

        return $process->getOutput();
    }
}

 FILE: server\app\Jobs\GenerateThumbnail.php [58 lines | 1.9 KB | php]
────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

<?php

namespace App\Jobs;

use App\Models\Screenshot;
use App\Services\Vault;
use Illuminate\Contracts\Queue\ShouldQueue;
use Illuminate\Foundation\Queue\Queueable;
use Illuminate\Support\Str;

class GenerateThumbnail implements ShouldQueue
{
    use Queueable;

    public int $tries = 3;

    public function __construct(public string $screenshotId) {}

    public function backoff(): array
    {
        return [15, 60, 180];
    }

    public function handle(Vault $vault): void
    {
        $shot = Screenshot::find($this->screenshotId);
        if (! $shot || $shot->thumbnail_path) {
            return;
        }
        $source = $vault->get($shot->path, $shot->storage);
        $size = @getimagesizefromstring($source);
        // Keep large multi-monitor originals viewable without decoding them in GD.
        if (! $size || $size[0] * $size[1] > 16000000) {
            return;
        }
        $image = imagecreatefromstring($source);
        unset($source);
        if (! $image) {
            throw new \RuntimeException('Thumbnail image could not be decoded.');
        }
        $width = min(480, imagesx($image));
        $height = max(1, (int) round(imagesy($image) * $width / imagesx($image)));
        $thumbnail = imagecreatetruecolor($width, $height);
        imagecopyresampled($thumbnail, $image, 0, 0, 0, 0, $width, $height, imagesx($image), imagesy($image));
        ob_start();
        imagejpeg($thumbnail, null, 75);
        $bytes = ob_get_clean();
        imagedestroy($thumbnail);
        imagedestroy($image);
        // Each attempt owns its file; only the first conditional publication wins.
        $path = 'thumbnails/'.$shot->device_id.'/'.$shot->id.'-'.Str::uuid().'.jpg';
        $vault->put($path, $bytes, $shot->storage);
        if (! Screenshot::whereKey($shot->id)->whereNull('thumbnail_path')->update(['thumbnail_path' => $path])) {
            $vault->delete($path, $shot->storage);
        }
    }
}

<?php

namespace App\Http\Middleware;

use Closure;
use Illuminate\Http\Request;
use Symfony\Component\HttpFoundation\Response;

class AdminAccess
{
    public function handle(Request $request, Closure $next, string $role = 'reviewer'): Response
    {
        $user = $request->user();
        abort_unless($user && $user->enabled, 403, 'This account is disabled.');
        abort_unless(in_array($user->role, ['super_admin', 'reviewer'], true), 403, 'Administrator access required.');
        if ($role === 'super_admin') {
            abort_unless($user->role === 'super_admin', 403, 'Super admin access required.');
        }

        return $next($request);
    }
}

<?php

namespace App\Http\Middleware;

use App\Models\Device;
use Closure;
use Illuminate\Http\Request;
use Symfony\Component\HttpFoundation\Response;

class DeviceAccess
{
    public function handle(Request $request, Closure $next): Response
    {
        $user = $request->user();
        $token = $user?->currentAccessToken();
        abort_unless($user && $user->enabled && $user->role === 'employee' && $token && isset($token->id) && $token->can('device:collect'), 403, 'Device access revoked.');
        $device = Device::where('token_id', $token->id)->where('user_id', $user->id)->first();
        abort_unless($device && ! $device->disabled_at, 403, 'Device access revoked.');
        $request->attributes->set('device', $device);

        return $next($request);
    }
}

<?php

namespace App\Http\Controllers;

use App\Services\Audit;
use Illuminate\Http\JsonResponse;
use Illuminate\Http\Request;
use Illuminate\Support\Facades\Auth;
use Illuminate\Validation\ValidationException;

class AdminAuthController extends Controller
{
    public function login(Request $request): JsonResponse
    {
        $data = $request->validate(['email' => 'required|email', 'password' => 'required|string']);
        if (! Auth::attempt([...$data, 'enabled' => true])) {
            throw ValidationException::withMessages(['email' => 'Invalid email or password.']);
        }
        if (! in_array($request->user()->role, ['super_admin', 'reviewer'], true)) {
            Auth::logout();
            throw ValidationException::withMessages(['email' => 'Use the desktop agent for employee login.']);
        }
        $request->session()->regenerate();
        Audit::record($request, 'admin.login');

        return response()->json(['user' => $request->user()]);
    }

    public function me(Request $request): JsonResponse
    {
        return response()->json(['user' => $request->user()]);
    }

    public function logout(Request $request): JsonResponse
    {
        Audit::record($request, 'admin.logout');
        Auth::logout();
        $request->session()->invalidate();
        $request->session()->regenerateToken();

        return response()->json(['success' => true]);
    }
}

<?php

namespace App\Http\Controllers;

use App\Models\ActivityLog;
use App\Models\AuditLog;
use App\Models\Device;
use App\Models\MonitoringPolicy;
use App\Models\Screenshot;
use App\Models\User;
use App\Services\Audit;
use App\Services\Vault;
use Carbon\CarbonImmutable;
use Illuminate\Database\Eloquent\Builder;
use Illuminate\Http\JsonResponse;
use Illuminate\Http\Request;
use Illuminate\Support\Facades\DB;
use Illuminate\Validation\Rule;
use Illuminate\Validation\Rules\Password;
use Symfony\Component\HttpFoundation\Response;

class AdminController extends Controller
{
    public function overview(Request $request): JsonResponse
    {
        Audit::record($request, 'overview.view');

        return response()->json(['devices' => Device::count(), 'online' => Device::whereNull('disabled_at')->where('last_seen_at', '>=', now()->subMinutes(2))->count(), 'employees' => User::where('role', 'employee')->where('enabled', true)->count(), 'screenshots_today' => Screenshot::where('captured_at', '>=', now()->startOfDay())->count(), 'recent_devices' => Device::with('user:id,name')->orderByDesc('last_seen_at')->limit(6)->get(), 'apps' => ActivityLog::where('captured_at', '>=', now()->startOfDay())->select('app_name')->selectRaw('COUNT(*) AS samples')->groupBy('app_name')->orderByDesc('samples')->limit(6)->get()]);
    }

    public function options(): JsonResponse
    {
        return response()->json(['users' => User::where('role', 'employee')->orderBy('name')->get(['id', 'name']), 'devices' => Device::orderBy('name')->get(['id', 'name'])]);
    }

    public function users(Request $request): JsonResponse
    {
        Audit::record($request, 'users.list');

        return response()->json(User::orderByDesc('created_at')->paginate(20));
    }

    public function createUser(Request $request): JsonResponse
    {
        $data = $request->validate(['name' => 'required|string|max:120', 'email' => 'required|email|max:255|unique:users,email', 'role' => ['required', Rule::in(['super_admin', 'reviewer', 'employee'])], 'password' => ['required', 'string', Password::min(12)]]);
        $data['email'] = strtolower($data['email']);
        $user = User::create($data);
        Audit::record($request, 'user.created', 'user', $user->id, ['role' => $user->role]);

        return response()->json($user, 201);
    }

    public function updateUser(Request $request, User $user): JsonResponse
    {
        $data = $request->validate(['enabled' => 'required|boolean']);
        abort_if($user->id === $request->user()->id && ! $data['enabled'], 422, 'You cannot disable your own account.');
        DB::transaction(function () use ($user, $data): void {
            $locked = User::whereKey($user->id)->lockForUpdate()->firstOrFail();
            $locked->update($data);
            if (! $data['enabled']) {
                $locked->tokens()->delete();
                $locked->devices()->update(['disabled_at' => now(), 'token_id' => null]);
                DB::table('sessions')->where('user_id', $locked->id)->delete();
            }
        });
        Audit::record($request, $data['enabled'] ? 'user.enabled' : 'user.disabled', 'user', $user->id);

        return response()->json($user->fresh());
    }

    public function devices(Request $request): JsonResponse
    {
        Audit::record($request, 'devices.list');

        return response()->json(Device::with('user:id,name,email')->orderByDesc('created_at')->paginate(20));
    }

    public function updateDevice(Request $request, Device $device): JsonResponse
    {
        $data = $request->validate(['enabled' => 'sometimes|boolean', 'paused' => 'sometimes|boolean']);
        abort_if(! $data, 422, 'No change supplied.');
        DB::transaction(function () use ($device, $data): void {
            $locked = Device::whereKey($device->id)->lockForUpdate()->firstOrFail();
            if (array_key_exists('enabled', $data)) {
                $locked->disabled_at = $data['enabled'] ? null : now();
                if (! $data['enabled']) {
                    $locked->user->tokens()->whereKey($locked->token_id)->delete();
                    $locked->token_id = null;
                }
            }
            if (array_key_exists('paused', $data)) {
                $locked->paused = $data['paused'];
            }
            $locked->save();
        });
        Audit::record($request, 'device.updated', 'device', $device->id, $data);

        return response()->json($device->fresh());
    }

    public function policy(): JsonResponse
    {
        return response()->json(['policy' => MonitoringPolicy::current(), 'storage' => config('tracker.storage')]);
    }

    public function savePolicy(Request $request): JsonResponse
    {
        $data = $request->validate(['monitoring_enabled' => 'required|boolean', 'screenshot_interval_seconds' => 'required|integer|min:30|max:3600', 'activity_interval_seconds' => 'required|integer|min:5|max:300', 'browser_urls' => 'required|boolean', 'retention_days' => 'required|integer|min:1|max:365', 'audit_retention_days' => 'required|integer|min:30|max:3650', 'offline_queue_max_mb' => 'required|integer|min:50|max:10240', 'offline_retention_days' => 'required|integer|min:1|max:30', 'notice' => 'required|string|min:20|max:4000']);
        $policy = DB::transaction(function () use ($data): MonitoringPolicy {
            $policy = MonitoringPolicy::whereKey(MonitoringPolicy::current()->id)->lockForUpdate()->firstOrFail();
            $policy->fill($data);
            $policy->version++;
            $policy->save();

            return $policy;
        });
        Audit::record($request, 'policy.updated', 'policy', '1', ['version' => $policy->version, 'changed_fields' => array_keys($data)]);

        return response()->json(['policy' => $policy]);
    }

    public function storageCheck(Request $request, Vault $vault): JsonResponse
    {
        try {
            $vault->check();
        } catch (\Throwable $exception) {
            report($exception);
            Audit::record($request, 'storage.check_failed');

            return response()->json(['message' => 'Storage check failed. Inspect server credentials, certificate trust, connectivity and folder permissions.'], 503);
        }
        Audit::record($request, 'storage.checked');

        return response()->json(['message' => 'Storage write, read and delete checks passed.']);
    }

    public function screenshots(Request $request): JsonResponse
    {
        $query = $this->filtered(Screenshot::query(), $request)->with('device.user')->orderByDesc('captured_at')->orderBy('id');
        Audit::record($request, 'screenshots.list', null, null, $request->only('user_id', 'device_id', 'from', 'to', 'app'));

        return response()->json($query->paginate(24)->through(fn (Screenshot $shot) => [
            'id' => $shot->id, 'captured_at' => $shot->captured_at, 'app_name' => $shot->app_name, 'window_title' => $shot->window_title,
            'device_name' => $shot->device->name, 'user_name' => $shot->device->user->name, 'image_url' => route('screenshot.file', $shot, false),
            'thumbnail_url' => route('screenshot.thumbnail', $shot, false),
        ]));
    }

    public function image(Request $request, Screenshot $screenshot, Vault $vault): Response
    {
        $thumb = $request->routeIs('screenshot.thumbnail') && $screenshot->thumbnail_path;
        Audit::record($request, $thumb ? 'screenshot.thumbnail_viewed' : 'screenshot.viewed', 'screenshot', $screenshot->id, ['device_id' => $screenshot->device_id]);
        try {
            $bytes = $vault->get($thumb ? $screenshot->thumbnail_path : $screenshot->path, $screenshot->storage);
        } catch (\Throwable $error) {
            report($error);
            abort(503, 'Screenshot storage is unavailable.');
        }

        return response($bytes, 200, ['Content-Type' => $thumb ? 'image/jpeg' : 'image/png', 'Cache-Control' => 'private, no-store', 'X-Content-Type-Options' => 'nosniff', 'Content-Disposition' => 'inline; filename="screenshot.'.($thumb ? 'jpg' : 'png').'"']);
    }

    public function activity(Request $request): JsonResponse
    {
        Audit::record($request, 'activity.list', null, null, $request->only('user_id', 'device_id', 'from', 'to', 'app'));

        return response()->json($this->filtered(ActivityLog::query(), $request)->with('device.user')->orderByDesc('captured_at')->orderBy('id')->paginate(50)->through(fn (ActivityLog $event) => [
            'id' => $event->id, 'captured_at' => $event->captured_at, 'app_name' => $event->app_name, 'window_title' => $event->window_title, 'url' => $event->url,
            'device_name' => $event->device->name, 'user_name' => $event->device->user->name,
        ]));
    }

    public function export(Request $request): Response
    {
        if (! $request->filled('from')) {
            $request->merge(['from' => now()->toDateString()]);
        }
        if (! $request->filled('to')) {
            $request->merge(['to' => $request->input('from')]);
        }
        $query = $this->filtered(ActivityLog::query(), $request)->with('device.user')->orderBy('captured_at');
        abort_if(CarbonImmutable::parse($request->input('from'))->diffInDays(CarbonImmutable::parse($request->input('to'))) > 31, 422, 'Export at most 31 days at a time.');
        abort_if($query->count() > 100000, 422, 'Narrow this export to fewer than 100,000 records.');
        Audit::record($request, 'activity.exported', null, null, $request->only('user_id', 'device_id', 'from', 'to', 'app'));

        return response()->streamDownload(function () use ($query): void {
            $stream = fopen('php://output', 'w');
            fputcsv($stream, ['Captured at (UTC)', 'Employee', 'Device', 'Application', 'Window title', 'Browser address'], ',', '"', '');
            foreach ($query->lazy(500) as $event) {
                $values = [$event->captured_at->toIso8601String(), $event->device->user->name, $event->device->name, $event->app_name, $event->window_title, $event->url ?? ''];
                fputcsv($stream, array_map(static fn (string $value) => preg_match('/^[=+\-@\t\r\n]/', $value) ? "'".$value : $value, $values), ',', '"', '');
            }
            fclose($stream);
        }, 'activity.csv', ['Content-Type' => 'text/csv; charset=UTF-8', 'Cache-Control' => 'no-store']);
    }

    public function audit(Request $request): JsonResponse
    {
        Audit::record($request, 'audit.list');

        return response()->json(AuditLog::with('actor:id,name')->orderByDesc('id')->paginate(50));
    }

    private function filtered(Builder $query, Request $request): Builder
    {
        $filters = $request->validate(['user_id' => 'nullable|uuid', 'device_id' => 'nullable|uuid', 'from' => 'nullable|date_format:Y-m-d', 'to' => ['nullable', 'date_format:Y-m-d', Rule::when($request->filled('from'), 'after_or_equal:from')], 'app' => 'nullable|string|max:160', 'search' => 'nullable|string|max:200']);
        if (! empty($filters['user_id'])) {
            $query->whereHas('device', fn (Builder $device) => $device->where('user_id', $filters['user_id']));
        }
        if (! empty($filters['device_id'])) {
            $query->where('device_id', $filters['device_id']);
        }
        if (! empty($filters['from'])) {
            $query->where('captured_at', '>=', CarbonImmutable::parse($filters['from'])->startOfDay());
        }
        if (! empty($filters['to'])) {
            $query->where('captured_at', '<=', CarbonImmutable::parse($filters['to'])->endOfDay());
        }
        if (! empty($filters['app'])) {
            $query->whereRaw("app_name LIKE ? ESCAPE '!'", ['%'.str_replace(['!', '%', '_'], ['!!', '!%', '!_'], $filters['app']).'%']);
        }
        if (! empty($filters['search'])) {
            $query->whereRaw("window_title LIKE ? ESCAPE '!'", ['%'.str_replace(['!', '%', '_'], ['!!', '!%', '!_'], $filters['search']).'%']);
        }

        return $query;
    }
}
